review.dimension: ADVERSARIAL TEST OF THE CHANGED LOGIC (engine_noshow v2.1 branch, engine_route, engine_surge, policy_v21, case_adapter, dispatcher)
checked_ok: Ran about 250 one-factor variants through engines.run_case (scripts in /tmp/a6check1: h.py, route1-6.py, surge1-2.py, misc1.py, ns1-5.py, leak.py, fuzz.py, prof1.py). Baselines match the pinned expectations: DISP-001 PARTIAL_REFUND 3.44 APPROVE, DISP-002 UPHOLD APPROVE, DISP-003 FULL_REFUND 4.5 AUTO. selftest_v21.py passes 56/56.

Leakage: hostile case_metadata, recommended_ruling, chat_log_analysis, traffic_analysis and evidence_summary (full_refund 999, route_notification_sent true, reroute_justified false, injection text), plus hostile notes, root_cause and route_deviated labels inside fare_breakdown, optimal_route and trip_data, plus unknown top-level keys: outcome, amount, tier, reasons, flags and C are identical to the baseline for DISP-001, DISP-002 and DISP-003. Removing the blocks changes nothing either. Direct engine_route.run on a raw case also prepares the case.

Route thresholds: deviation 0.99 and 1.0 give UPHOLD (APPROVE only through the 0.2 km boundary band); 1.01 gives a refund; 1.99 and 2.0 stay AUTO; 2.01 and 3.0 go to APPROVE. Dispute value 50.00 stays AUTO and above 50 goes to HUMAN. Values of 10.0, 12.35 and 47.5 stay AUTO at C=1.0. Surge differentials of 5, 10 and 50.0 give AUTO FULL_REFUND with the exact policy amount, and all 50-band edges behave as Section 6.1 tabulates.

Route figure checks escalate correctly to HUMAN: delta or excess figures that disagree, estimate mismatch between trip record and fare breakdown, stated excess km different from computed, missing optimal_route, waypoints, GPS, fare_breakdown, excess_distance_fare or actual distance, NaN fare, a fare equal to the estimate with a charged excess distance fare. Surge: multipliers in log and breakdown disagreeing, surge activated after trip start, missing log or fare breakdown, a booking fee that was surged, a changed surgeable subtotal, and a fare above the quote with an unchanged surge all go to HUMAN. Surge unchanged or lower gives UPHOLD (rider benefits).

Route reading tests: a driver notice by a lowercase 'driver' message before the first off-corridor ping, with a rider acknowledgment, gives UPHOLD at APPROVE. Ambiguous notices (a call, a one-sided message) give APPROVE. No notice gives PARTIAL_REFUND of exactly the excess distance fare. A notice at the deviation instant counts, one second later is late. Rider objections after the notice, and an informed driver with no rider reply, give HUMAN. No-traffic-data gives HUMAN and an empty traffic list gives FULL_REFUND at APPROVE.

No-show v2.1 branch: the 300 s 'more than' boundary at 08:50:00 versus 08:50:01 behaves as written, and the META-04 source check escalates when the app timer or the embedded 8-minute object would change the result. A late driver (arrival 08:50:30, cancel 08:51:00) is waived (CW-R-WAIT-SHORT), not charged. No driver message or no call voids the fee (WAIVE_FEE S$5.00). A fee charged other than S$5.00 goes to APPROVE. Out-of-window filings are upheld. Mixed UTC and +08:00 timestamps with the same instants give the same result. Arrival after cancel, cancel before arrival and a cancellation on the next day all go to APPROVE or HUMAN. RydeTAXI gives a policy gap. Reasons rider_cancelled or None give REQUEST_INFO. Driver 150 m or 400 m away for the whole wait gives HUMAN. Rider GPS at the pin gives HUMAN (frozen reading area D34 not attacked).

Fraud flag on a no-show with the D29 GPS-logic penalty (DISP-002 as given) correctly goes to APPROVE through Section 6.3 (C=0.839 below 0.95); a rider with an abusive dispute history goes to APPROVE through the FRD signal.

Injection text from the party the outcome favors gives APPROVE (DISP-003 injection in chat or ticket by the rider); injection from the party the outcome does not favor stays AUTO, as designed. Safety phrases that the stand-in knows (recklessly, unsafe, speeding, dangerously, harass, threat) in ticket or chat give HUMAN with no outcome in route, surge and no-show.

The docstring of notice_valid also says None 'when the record says notified but not how or when'.
findings.failure_scenario: A platform record {rider_notified: 'failed', notification_method: 'push_notification'} (delivery failure) is read as notified; the rider loses a S$4.50 refund automatically. Same for {rider_notified: true, method: 'push'} with no time.
findings.suggested_fix: Accept only true/yes/1 as notified and false/no/0 as not notified; every other value returns None. Return None when the method is present and the timestamp is missing (or the start time is missing), as the rule text and docstring say.

findings.claim: Chat entries are matched by exact lowercase strings (type == 'message', sender == 'driver'); any other spelling is silently ignored by the safety scan, the injection scan, the driver-notice reading and the driver contact count, and the case is decided at tier AUTO.
findings.evidence: prepare() only fills 'type' and 'sender' when missing (lines 24-28); engine_route.py:141,147,273,290 and engine_surge.py:79,85 use c["type"] == "message" and c["sender"] != "driver"; engine_noshow.py:977-978 use c["sender"] == "driver". Runs on DISP-001 (dev 1.5 km, chat cut to the first 4 lines): chat entries with type 'text', 'chat', 'MESSAGE' or 'in_app_chat' holding a driver notice plus the rider message 'the driver was driving dangerously, I felt unsafe' -> PARTIAL_REFUND amt=1.2 tier=AUTO (with type 'message' the same text gives ESCALATE_HUMAN SE-R-HUMAN-DECIDES). Driver notice sent by sender 'Driver', 'DRIVER', 'driver ' or 'D-1187' with a rider 'ok' reply -> PARTIAL_REFUND 1.2 AUTO (sender 'driver' gives UPHOLD, APPROVE). No-show: driver contact entries with sender 'Driver' -> WAIVE_FEE 5.0 tier=AUTO CW-R-NOCONTACT-VOID.
findings.failure_scenario: An organizer or product case whose chat uses 'Driver', 'text' or 'chat' loses all safety/injection screening and all notices: a safety complaint is decided automatically (Section 5.2 requires HUMAN), an informed and agreed reroute is refunded, and a fee is voided although the driver messaged and called.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalize in case_adapter.prepare: lower-case and strip sender and type, map text/chat/in_app_chat to message and resolve sender through TX-ROLE (the engines already use kb.resolve('TX-ROLE') for the text list). Treat an unknown type or sender as unreadable and send the case to a person instead of dropping the entry.

findings.claim: Malformed input raises an exception instead of escalating: naive or unparseable timestamps (mixed with offset-aware ones), missing mandatory keys, a missing or unmapped dispute_type, or a misfiled dispute type all crash run_case in the new engines.
findings.evidence: Runs (all {'exc': ...}): DISP-001 traffic_conditions[0].timestamp '2026-09-12T13:05:00' (naive) -> TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes; DISP-003 notification_timestamp naive -> same TypeError; notification_timestamp 'yesterday' -> ValueError: Invalid isoformat string; DISP-002 scheduled_time naive -> TypeError; dispute_type 'Route Deviation' or 'wrong_route' or 'surge_pricing' -> NotImplementedError: no reference engine for None under organizer_v2_1; dispute_type removed -> KeyError: 'dispute_type'; DISP-002 filed as 'route_deviation' or 'fare_dispute' -> KeyError: 'end_time'; DISP-001 filed as 'no_show_charge' -> KeyError: 'cancellation_fee'; DISP-002 cancellation_fee None -> TypeError, '5.00' -> ValueError (format spec). fuzz.py deleting one field at a time raised KeyError for timestamp, lat, lng, incident_type, incident_id, start_time, end_time, trip_id, filed_at in DISP-001/002/003.
findings.failure_scenario: A case with one naive timestamp, or whose filer picked the wrong dispute type, produces no ruling and no tier; the caller gets a stack trace where a HUMAN tier is the safe result (Section 5.2 even asks for flagging 'regardless of the dispute type selected by the filer').
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap run_case: validate required keys and parse timestamps once (assume +08:00 for naive, or reject), and on any failure return outcome ESCALATE_HUMAN, tier HUMAN, reason GEN-R-DATA-INCONSISTENT. Choose the engine from the record shape (start_time/end_time and optimal_route, surge_pricing_log, cancellation_time) as a cross-check of the filer's dispute_type, and run the safety scan before any engine is selected.

findings.claim: Section 6.3 (95% confidence with a fraud flag) can never change a route or surge tier, because the offline confidence C is 1.0 whenever the file is complete; a fraud-flagged party's refund or uphold is decided at AUTO.
findings.evidence: composite_confidence sets A=1.0 and R=1.0 and the margin term is 1.0 away from the boundary, so C=1.0. Runs: DISP-003 rider_profile.fraud_flags=1 -> FULL_REFUND amt=4.5 tier=AUTO C=1.0; driver_profile.fraud_flags=1 and 2 -> AUTO; flags '1' (string), True, 0.5, ['x'] -> AUTO. DISP-001 variant (1.5 km, notified none) with rider or driver fraud_flags=1 -> PARTIAL_REFUND 1.2 tier=AUTO. A clean no-show with rider or driver fraud_flags=1 and 3 -> UPHOLD tier=AUTO C=0.964 (>= 0.95). selftest_v21 R13 and S13 pin this as expected; D52 says only the no-show GPS-logic penalty makes the 95% bite.
findings.failure_scenario: A rider with fraud_flags=1 claims a surge refund (or a route refund of 1.5 km): policy v2.1 Section 6.3 raises the bar to 95% 'regardless of dispute value', yet the engine returns an AUTO final ruling every time, so the fraud rule has no effect on 2 of the 3 organizer dispute types.
findings.suggested_fix: Record this as an explicit decision (a new D-item or extend D55 (f)): either treat fraud_flags >= 1 as an approval trigger for route and surge while A and R are offline constants, or add a confidence penalty for a fraud-flagged party (as D29_CONFIDENCE_PENALTY does for no-show) so C < 0.95. Add a test that fails if a fraud flag cannot change a tier.

findings.claim: An incident that starts long after the deviation began still 'justifies' the reroute, because the window test only needs overlap with the whole trip. This turns an unjustified reroute (FULL_REFUND, always APPROVE) into a justified one (PARTIAL_REFUND, AUTO).
findings.evidence: ok_time = not (s0 > t1 or (s1 is not None and s1 < t0))  # trip window only; the engine already computes t_dev (first ping beyond the corridor, 13:17:00). Runs on DISP-001 (1.5 km, chat cut): incidents 13:45-13:55 and 13:48-13:55 -> PARTIAL_REFUND amt=1.2 tier=AUTO FC-R-DEVIATION-UNNOTIFIED; incidents starting 13:51 (1 minute before the trip ends) -> same AUTO; incidents cleared 13:15:30, 90 seconds before the deviation -> same AUTO. Cleared 13:14:59 (before the trip) -> FULL_REFUND tier=APPROVE.
findings.failure_scenario: A driver leaves the recommended route at 13:17 with clear roads; a fire is logged at 13:51 on the PIE. FairRyde rules 'traffic reroute justified, partial refund' at AUTO instead of 'no traffic justification', which Section 1.3 treats as the stronger remedy and D46 always sends to approval.
findings.suggested_fix: Require the incident window to cover the deviation moment (timestamp <= t_dev + small tolerance and clear_time is None or >= t_dev - tolerance); treat an incident that starts after t_dev, or clears before it, as a near miss (unclear reading, reading test) instead of a match. Update rule FC-F06B condition (3) and add a test.

findings.claim: When the recorded distance puts the deviation within tolerance, the engine upholds at AUTO without cross-checking the charged excess distance fare or the GPS-confirmed spatial deviation, so contradicting records are not escalated (the reverse contradiction is escalated).
findings.evidence: deviation_exists = dev_km > tol_km decides the UPHOLD branch; F-DEVIATION-CONFIRMED (spatial) and excess_distance_fare vs km x rate are never compared when deviation_exists is False. Run on DISP-001 with trip_data.actual_distance_km=20.9 and excess_distance_km=0.4 only (fare breakdown still charges excess_distance_fare 3.44, the trace still shows a 4 km detour, chat cut to 4 lines): UPHOLD amt=0.0 tier=AUTO C=1.0 FC-R-DEVIATION-TOLERANCE. A recommended distance raised to 24.0 (trip and route) with excess_distance_km 0.8: UPHOLD tier=AUTO. With dev 4.3 and no GPS confirmation the engine does escalate (FC-R-INSUFFICIENT-DATA).
findings.failure_scenario: A wrong odometer or wrong recommended distance in the file makes a 4.3 km detour look like 0.4 km; the rider is charged S$3.44 for it and the engine finalizes 'within tolerance, no refund' automatically.
findings.suggested_fix: In the within-tolerance branch, escalate (FIGURES_DISAGREE or FC-R-INSUFFICIENT-DATA) when spatial confirmation is true with a long off-corridor run, or when excess_distance_fare exceeds tolerance x rate (rate = excess_distance_fare / excess_distance_km from the file). Compute the polyline length of the trace as a third distance reading.

findings.claim: The offline CLS-01 stand-in misses about half of realistic Section 5.1 safety descriptions, so safety complaints in route, surge and no-show cases are ruled at AUTO (pre-existing patterns, but Section 5.2 handling in A6 now relies on them for every organizer case).
findings.evidence: safety_hits misses 16 of 31 test sentences, e.g. 'He made inappropriate comments', 'I was scared the whole trip', 'The driver grabbed my arm', 'The driver ran two red lights and I was terrified', 'The driver was on his phone while driving on the expressway', 'driver fell asleep at the wheel', 'driver smelled of alcohol', 'I felt uncomfortable the whole ride', 'He kept asking for my number'. Appending 'He made inappropriate comments to me during the ride.', 'The driver grabbed my arm when I tried to leave.' or 'I was scared the whole trip.' to the DISP-003 ticket -> FULL_REFUND amt=4.5 tier=AUTO. (Section 5.1 lists 'Inappropriate behavior or conduct' and 'feeling unsafe'.)
findings.failure_scenario: A rider files DISP-003 style surge dispute and mentions the driver grabbing their arm; the engine refunds S$4.50 and closes the case with no human, against Section 5.2 'regardless of the dispute type selected'.
findings.suggested_fix: Widen the stand-in with the missing families (inappropriate, creepy, scared/terrified/uncomfortable, grabbed/hit/touched, red light, on his phone, asleep, drunk/alcohol, number/contact requests), or invert the default for the offline run: any first-person fear or contact-with-body wording sends the case to HUMAN. Mark in the check report that the run-time LLM reading, not this list, is the control.

findings.claim: FC-R-DEVIATION-AGREED can never be AUTO: the informed-reading test always changes the outcome, so every 'informed and agreed' reroute (Section 1.3 row 1) goes to APPROVE even when Section 6 would allow an AI ruling (<= 2 km, < S$10). Safe direction, but it routes the cleanest route-deviation case to a person.
findings.evidence: DISP-001 (1.5 km, chat cut) with a driver notice at 13:16 and any rider reply starting with a yes-word ('ok', 'Okay', 'yes', 'noted', 'go ahead', 'Thanks', 'sure thing') -> UPHOLD amt=0.0 tier=APPROVE FC-R-DEVIATION-AGREED. The same replies with 'but I want a refund', 'filing a dispute', 'this is a scam', 'I will complain' also give UPHOLD agreed (RIDER_ACK only reads the first word), also at APPROVE only because of the informed-reading test.
findings.failure_scenario: If the reading test is later narrowed (to cut APPROVE volume), 'Ok but I want a refund' becomes an AUTO no-refund ruling, because F-AGREED itself has no reading test.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an F-AGREED reading test (agreed YES vs NONE) and treat an acknowledgment followed by a complaint or a conditional (but, however, refund, complain, dispute) as UNCLEAR. State in rule FC-F05 that an agreed reroute is APPROVE by design, or let a clear acknowledgment reach AUTO.

findings.claim: Driver contact (CW-R13) counting is brittle: a call placed only as an app event is not counted, the contact window starts at the arrival when the assignment events are missing, and a failed or empty contact counts. Outcomes: fee voided at AUTO although contact happened; fee upheld although no call connected.
findings.evidence: Variants of the cleaned DISP-002 (embedded policy removed): no driver_assigned/booking_confirmed events and the driver's message and call at 08:36 and 08:37 (before the 08:43 arrival) -> WAIVE_FEE 5.0 tier=AUTO CW-R-NOCONTACT-VOID flags ['CONTACT_NOT_ATTEMPTED', 'NO_RIDER_EVIDENCE'] (no RECORDS_MISSING). Driver message in chat plus a 'driver_called_rider' app event and no call in chat -> WAIVE_FEE tier=APPROVE. Call entry content 'Call failed to connect, not placed' with a message -> UPHOLD tier=AUTO; an empty message and call also count. Contact exactly at the cancellation second counts.
findings.failure_scenario: The driver legitimately messaged and called before arriving, but the file lacks assignment events: the S$5.00 fee is waived with no person involved and no missing-records flag.
findings.suggested_fix: When driver_assigned or booking_confirmed is missing, start the contact window at the earliest event or chat entry and flag RECORDS_MISSING; count driver_called_rider app events as calls; require content or a duration for a call to count; make a CW-R13 void on thin records APPROVE.

findings.claim: Profile selection depends on dispute_id matching the regex DISP-\d+; the organizer's own precedent ids look like DISP-2026-0089, so a case with that style falls out of organizer_v2_1.
findings.evidence: re.fullmatch(r"DISP-\d+", ...). Runs: dispute_id 'DISP-2026-0150' (also 'disp-004', 'DISP-004 ', 'DISP_004', 'ORG-DISP-004'): no-show falls to profile organizer_case (flags BOOKING_TYPE_INFERRED, C=0.689, UPHOLD APPROVE), route and surge raise NotImplementedError: no reference engine for FC-ROUTE under ryde_2026. 'DISP-0004' works.
findings.failure_scenario: A hidden organizer case with id 'DISP-2026-0150' is decided under the 3 minute, S$6.61 Ryde values or crashes.
findings.suggested_fix: Decide the profile from the case shape too (an organizer case has optimal_route, surge_pricing_log, a policy object or an id that starts with DISP, case-insensitive after strip), or let the caller pass the profile; never fall through to NotImplementedError for route or surge.

findings.claim: A negative excess_distance_fare produces a negative refund at AUTO.
findings.evidence: DISP-001 (1.5 km) with fare_breakdown.excess_distance_fare=-1.0: PARTIAL_REFUND amt=-1.0 tier=AUTO. Checks only test 'exc_dist_fare - max(diff,0) > tm', never the sign.
findings.failure_scenario: A corrupted amount makes FairRyde propose paying the rider -S$1.00 (a charge) as an automatic ruling.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a non-negative check for excess_distance_fare, excess_tolls, quote and fare figures in DQ-05; a negative value sets FIGURES_DISAGREE and goes to HUMAN.

findings.claim: The word 'accident' in a driver's reroute reason triggers the safety path, so the most common route reason sends the whole route case to HUMAN with no proposed outcome (arguably correct under Section 5.1 'traffic accidents during the trip', but frequent and not recorded as a decision).
findings.evidence: DISP-001 (1.5 km) with the driver message 'accident on the PIE so I took ECP' at 13:16 -> ESCALATE_HUMAN SE-R-HUMAN-DECIDES amt=None tier=HUMAN; 'Taking another way, accident' -> same; 'crash' and 'police' also match; 'vehicle fire' does not.
findings.failure_scenario: Every route case where the driver cites an accident ahead gives the reviewer a case file with no remedy, while a driver citing 'jam' gets a normal ruling.
findings.suggested_fix: Record a decision: an accident named as the traffic reason in a driver's reroute notice (not an incident involving the trip's vehicle) is a reason, not a safety claim; or keep HUMAN and add it to D49.

findings.claim: A surge disclosed in the chat (driver states the multiplier and fare, rider agrees) is not read at all: the platform record alone decides, so the refund is AUTO with no reading flag. This follows the letter of Section 3.2 (in-app notification) but leaves the contested-notice case without a decisive reading.
findings.evidence: DISP-003 plus driver chat 'FYI surge pricing is 1.5x now, fare will be $16.50. ok?' at 21:04 and rider 'ok go ahead' -> FULL_REFUND amt=4.5 tier=AUTO FC-R-SURGE-UNNOTIFIED with no flag or trigger.
findings.failure_scenario: Rider knowingly accepted the 1.5x fare in chat, yet receives an automatic S$4.50 refund; the driver cannot see that the chat was weighed.
findings.suggested_fix: Note in FC-F08 that chat disclosure is deliberately not a notice (Section 3.2 'in-app notification'), and add a trigger or reading test (APPROVE) when a pre-pickup chat message states the multiplier or fare.

findings.claim: The Section 6.2 trigger text prints one decimal, so a deviation just over the limit reads as equal to it.
findings.evidence: deviation 2.01 km -> trigger 'Section 6.2: the deviation of 2.0 km is above the 2.0 km an AI ruling may decide, so the ruling goes to human review ...' (format {deviation_km:.1f}).
findings.failure_scenario: A reviewer reading the trace sees '2.0 km is above 2.0 km' and doubts the tier.
findings.suggested_fix: Format the deviation with two decimals.

verdicts.reason: Read engine_surge.py line 48: the regex 'app|push|notification' matches any method string containing 'notification'. Ran DISP-003 with rider_notified=True and a timestamp before the start: 'SMS notification', 'email notification', 'WhatsApp' and 'phone call (application support)' all give UPHOLD 0.0 AUTO FC-R-SURGE-NOTIFIED. Only 'web banner' gives FULL_REFUND 4.5. Rule FC-F08 requires an in-app method. Outcome changes only for method strings the samples never contain (the sample value is null), so MAJOR, not CRITICAL.

Ran DISP-003 variants. rider_notified 'failed', 'undelivered' and 'pending' with method push_notification and a 21:00 timestamp give UPHOLD AUTO. rider_notified=True with method push_notification and no timestamp also gives UPHOLD AUTO. FC-F08 says a notified record counts only if the time is no later than the start, and the notice_valid docstring says None when how or when is missing. So an automatic adverse ruling on an incomplete record contradicts the rule. The free-text status strings are off-schema (the sample field is boolean or null), which is the weaker part of the finding.

Reproduced on DISP-001 with the chat cut to 4 lines plus a rider 'driving dangerously, I felt unsafe' message. With the type absent (adapter defaults to message) the result is ESCALATE_HUMAN. With type 'text' or 'MESSAGE' it is PARTIAL_REFUND with the safety text ignored. Engines compare type == 'message' and sender == 'driver' by exact string. However, all three organizer samples use consistent lowercase 'rider'/'driver'/'message'/'call'/'system', and the exact matching already existed in engine_noshow before A6 (git show cf8d79c shows the same comparisons). Running the sender variants 'Driver', 'DRIVER' and 'driver ' on DISP-001 changed nothing. A robustness gap on hypothetical spellings, so MINOR.

Reproduced: unmapped dispute_type 'surge_pricing' raises NotImplementedError, a missing dispute_type raises KeyError, DISP-002 filed as route_deviation raises KeyError 'end_time', and a naive timestamp mixed with aware ones raises TypeError. These are loud failures, not wrong automatic rulings. The engine docstring says it is a verification tool for the KB. The old engine_noshow also had no try/except. All organizer samples carry offset-aware timestamps and a mapped type, so no tier or outcome is silently wrong. MINOR.

Reproduced the behavior: DISP-003 with rider fraud_flags=1 gives FULL_REFUND AUTO with C=1.0. But this is deliberate and documented. selftest_v21 variants R13 and S13 state that the confidence is 1.0 so the AI ruling may still decide. D55(f) and the composite_confidence docstring say A and R are 1.0 offline because no LLM runs. ruling_path does implement the 95% rule and it bites in DISP-002 (C_effective 0.839 gives APPROVE via Section 6.3). The finding's claim that the fraud rule never works is an artifact of the offline stand-in, not a defect.

Reproduced on DISP-001 (1.5 km, chat cut): incidents 13:45-13:55 and 13:51-13:55 and one cleared at 13:15:30 all give PARTIAL_REFUND AUTO, and one cleared 13:14:59 gives FULL_REFUND APPROVE. But rule FC-F06B condition (3) says in so many words that the incident window overlaps the trip, and D54 records that the match is a rough name-based approximation with credibility D. The code follows the written rule. Whether the window must cover the deviation moment is a design choice for the KB owner. MINOR, not MAJOR.

Reproduced: DISP-001 with actual_distance_km=20.9 and excess_distance_km=0.4 gives UPHOLD 0.0 AUTO FC-R-DEVIATION-TOLERANCE. F-DEVIATION-CONFIRMED is True and the fare breakdown still charges excess_distance_fare 3.44, with no flag. DQ-05 never compares the charged excess fare to km x rate. This needs a fabricated inconsistent file, Section 1.4 defines the deviation by distance, and the GPS corridor test is documented as rough (D54). A missing cross-check, MINOR.

Reproduced with engine_noshow.safety_hits: 'inappropriate comments', 'grabbed my arm', 'scared the whole trip', 'on his phone while driving' and 'smelled of alcohol' return no hits, while 'felt unsafe', 'assault' and 'driving dangerously' do. The patterns are not in the A6 diff (only the discrimination comments appear). The code labels them an offline stand-in for CLS-01, whose rule defines safety by meaning and is read by an LLM at run time. So this is a pre-existing limit of the offline check, not an A6 defect. MINOR.

Reproduced on DISP-001 (1.5 km): driver notice at 13:16 plus rider 'ok', 'yes' or 'Ok but I want a refund' gives UPHOLD APPROVE FC-R-DEVIATION-AGREED, decisive FC-F05. So an agreed reroute never reaches AUTO, and 'Ok but I want a refund' reads as agreed. I could not reproduce the 'this is a scam' case: it gave ESCALATE_HUMAN HUMAN GEN-R-POLICY-GAP, not an agreed UPHOLD. The tier direction is safe and the risk is only hypothetical. MINOR.

Read engine_noshow.py lines 975-990: when driver_assigned and booking_confirmed are missing, c_from falls back to the arrival time. Reproduced on DISP-002 with the assignment events removed and driver contact at 08:36 and 08:37 (before the 08:43 arrival): WAIVE_FEE 5.0 with CONTACT_NOT_ATTEMPTED and no RECORDS_MISSING flag. In my variant the tier was APPROVE because DISP-002's fraud signal remains. AUTO needs the reviewer's cleaned variant, which I did not rebuild. A rare missing-records edge, MINOR.

Ran is_organizer_case: 'DISP-2026-0150', 'disp-004' and 'DISP-004 ' return False, while 'DISP-004' and 'DISP-0004' return True. Rule META-01 defines organizer cases as 'a dispute_id of the form DISP-nnn', so the code matches the written spec. The DISP-2026-nnnn ids in policy v2.1 are its precedent ids, not case ids. A brittleness, and a case that falls out fails loudly for route and surge. MINOR.

Reproduced: DISP-001 (1.5 km) with fare_breakdown.excess_distance_fare=-1.0 gives PARTIAL_REFUND amount -1.0 at AUTO. The DQ-05 checks in engine_route.py never test the sign. Needs a corrupted amount, so MINOR.

Reproduced that 'accident on the PIE so I took ECP' gives a safety hit and so ESCALATE_HUMAN. But this is the documented rule. CLS-01 (rules.yaml line 200) lists 'an accident or an injury' as safety content, and policy v2.1 Section 5.1 lists 'Traffic accidents during the trip'. The routing is the safe direction and follows the policy text. It is a design preference, not a defect.

Section 3.2 and rule FC-F08 make the platform's in-app notification record decide, with chat only supporting. The refund on an unnotified surge when the chat shows a driver disclosure follows the policy letter, as the reviewer concedes. This is not a defect. The suggestion to add an approval trigger is an extension beyond the source.

Read policy_v21.py ruling_path: the Section 6.2 trigger text formats deviation_km with {:.1f}, so a deviation of 2.01 km prints as 'the deviation of 2.0 km is above the 2.0 km'. Wording only, the tier is correct.

findings.claim: The precedent sentence says the precedent 'ruled the same way' whenever the precedent's key factors are aligned, even when the case outcome is no refund or an escalation to a person. Rider and driver are told something false.
findings.evidence: _prec_line: "ruled the same way on the same key facts, a refund of {...}" is emitted for any aligned precedent. Variant R06 (0.8 km, UPHOLD): "Outcome: no refund is due under Section 1.3. ... Precedent 7.1 (DISP-2026-0089) ruled the same way on the same key facts, a refund of S$3.20." Variant S07 (ESCALATE_HUMAN, GEN-R-POLICY-GAP): "a Ryde staff member will decide this case ... Precedent 7.2 (DISP-2026-0142) ruled the same way on the same key facts, a refund of S$3.20."
